text.tspan: I keep a short thread on this. Office hours
with a professor reminded me what good
teaching feels like.
I take messy notes and rewrite one clean page
within 24 hours.
My note back to the group was basically this.
Adult learning works when life logistics are
respected.
Writing it down so I do not forget.
Protect sleep even during exam weeks. Memory
needs it.
I take messy notes and rewrite one clean page
within 24 hours.
Schedule the study block before motivation
arrives.
A librarian helped me find sources I would
have missed entirely.
Being a beginner again is a professional
skill.
Office hours felt intimidating until I went
once and stayed going.
Ask the basic questions early.
I print the syllabus and highlight deadlines
like a project plan.
Teach back what you learn or you did not
really learn it.
Group projects taught me as much about
collaboration as content.
Choose programs for the problems you want to
solve, not the brand alone.
I explain new concepts out loud to an empty
room. It works.
Failure on a low-stakes quiz is cheap tuition.
A librarian helped me find sources I would
have missed entirely.
Education is a long game dressed up as short
assignments.
Group projects taught me as much about
collaboration as content.
